protocol.name: nidara_material_v1
protocol.description: A surface declares the shapes of its glass and how the compositor resolves them against what lies behind: the blur's size and passes, per surface. The shapes are exact (rounded rectangles whose corners are superellipse quadrants, the shell's squircle), so the blur never depends on the alpha of the surface's own pixels: a low-alpha shadow next to the glass is not blurred because it is not in a shape.

request.name: get_material

description.summary: the material object of a surface

request.description: One per wl_surface; the state is double-buffered on wl_surface.commit.

description.summary: remove the material on the next commit

request.name: add_shape
request.description: Surface-local, logical coordinates. corner_radius and exponent describe each corner: a superellipse quadrant of that radius (exponent 2 is a circular arc). Fixed-point values.

request.name: set_blur

description.summary: pending: blur size and passes for this surface

request.description: size is the kawase offset in logical pixels, passes the number of downsampling levels. passes 0 = no blur.

request.name: set_glass

description.summary: pending: the compositor paints the glass itself

request.description: The compositor resolves the whole glass against the real backdrop, per pixel: the blurred backdrop, refracted near the edge; its saturation; a tint whose opacity rises where the backdrop is bright so that content of target_luminance contrast stays legible, between alpha_min and alpha_max; and a specular rim. The client then paints only its content and state (active fills, hover), not the glass.

arg.name: target_luminance
arg.summary: the backdrop luminance, after tint, not to exceed

description.summary: pending: back to blur only; the client paints its glass
